profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, with work spanning climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. Ai2 is currently led by Ali Farhadi, and the organization describes its research as guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles oriented toward safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems.

Ai2 develops and maintains two notable AI products tracked by this site. OLMo is an open-source large language model built with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, consistent with the organization's nonprofit mission. Semantic Scholar is an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs, also developed with a nonprofit research focus.

The organization maintains active research partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the National Science Foundation (supporting the Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure to Accelerate Science project), and Google Cloud (supporting development of open AI models and platforms for scientific research and environmental modeling). No litigation, patent filings, or SEC records are held for this organization.
